source: GitHub Advisory OSV + GitHub Advisory API (malicious package detection)
description: Open-source supply-chain attacks: malicious npm/pypi packages with preinstall hooks, dependency confusion, credential exfiltration, or remote code execution payloads.

maliciousPackages.summary:
_-= Per source details. Do not edit below this line.=-_

The package ships a postinstall hook ("node beacon.cjs") and a main entry (index.js) that both execute beacon.cjs on npm install and on require(). beacon.cjs collects installer-side identifiers — os.hostname(), __dirname (the install path on the installer's disk), process.cwd(), process.version, and the package name — and POSTs them as JSON to the hardcoded endpoint https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc, a bare Contabo VPS unrelated to any documented publisher. The HTTPS request is made with rejectUnauthorized:false, disabling TLS certificate verification. index.js itself exports a Proxy whose properties all return no-op values, so the package provides no real functionality — the install-time and import-time beacon is the sole effect of installing this package. The shape (stub module + hardcoded bare-VPS callback + TLS verification disabled + auto-fire on both lifecycle hook and module load) matches a dependency-confusion / install-tracking beacon rather than a legitimate library.

The rest of the module surface is a Proxy returning no-op functions so a consuming build does not crash. The destination is not associated with the `@c1-ease` scope's publisher, the beacon fires without caller opt-in on both install and import, and an in-source comment frames a completed build-with-callback as evidence of reach — consistent with a dependency-confusion / namespace-squat probe against internal `@c1-ease/*` package names.
